newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal copper workers say strike to continue.
newsitem.headline: Portugal copper workers say strike to continue.

text.p: Strike leaders at Portugal's Neves Corvo copper mine said the stoppage would continue despite company assertions that production had resumed on Thursday afternoon.

"The strike goes on," said union leader Eduardo Lazaro after Somincor, the state-owned firm that operates the mine, said that partial output had begun again after of busloads of strikers went to Lisbon to press their demands at the company's headquarters and at the Economy Ministry.

Lazaro, who said he was skeptical of the company's statement that output had been resumed at 80 percent, told Reuters that pickets would be outside the mine near Beja in southern Portugal before the morning shift began at 0500 GMT Friday.
The company has blamed the picketing for preventing miners wanting to ignore the strike, which began on Monday over working hours, from getting to work.
Earlier, a spokeswoman for the company told Reuters that output had resumed during the afternoon after busloads of miners left for the capital.
"Their numbers cannot be right," Lazaro said when asked to comment on the statement about output.
Some engineers and foremen might have gone into the mine but there were no miners amongst them, he said. "It is not possible to return to that level of production with so few people," he said.
But according to the company, some 75 miners had reported for duty, over 50 percent of the afternoon shift at the mine, which produced 107,000 tonnes of copper in 1996.
Miners are protesting at the company's imposing of Sunday working at the mine, where copper yields have been falling steadily in recent years.
The company says that it is willing to talk but will not retreat on the question of seven-day operations which it says are vital to the mine remaining competitive.
Miners leaders met representatives of the company and the ministry in Lisbon but no progress was made in resolving the dispute, Lazaro said.
